clue.text: About to fit into shoe, which is an outrage

indicators.note: one thing made to fit into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a sandal is a kind of open shoe
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone is scandalised that a shoe has been squeezed onto a foot it does not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public disgrace or affront that provokes general indignation, which is what an outrage is.

clue.text: Footballers otherwise featured in endless chat

indicators.note: something featured in a thing appears within it
without an end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
or else means otherwise

explanation.surface: Players crop up as the topic of some idle talk that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footballers' names a team rather than players in general: Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC is a Premier League club, so its players can be named collectively by the club's name.

clue.text: Blue-blooded brave

blocks.note: first meaning: of aristocratic birth
second meaning: showing fine, courageous character

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with courage, described in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both high-born aristocratic rank and lofty, courageous qualities of character.

clue.text: Recklessness gets a group functioning

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group, of musicians for instance
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A band starts playing with wild, careless energy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, abandon means a complete lack of inhibition or restraint, as in dancing with wild abandon.

clue.text: Margie holds a penny back: that's witty

definitions.note: a description standing for a noun: something that is witty

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside
going back means the result is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A woman called Margie pockets a coin and keeps it, which someone finds amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes between MARGI and E, and the whole is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, clever, pointed saying, so it is a thing whose essence is its wit.

clue.text: Supple one cutting plant

indicators.note: something cutting into a word splits it and sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gardener takes a cutting from a bendy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something flexible that bends easily without breaking.

clue.text: The blouse that took the biscuit!

blocks.note: first meaning: a loose red shirt like those of the Italian patriot's Redshirts
second meaning: a flat biscuit with a layer of squashed currants

explanation.surface: An outrageous blouse that beat everything for awfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the biscuit is a British idiom meaning to be the most outrageous; here it literally joins a blouse and a biscuit sharing one name, both from the Italian general.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the women's red blouse and the currant biscuit were named after the Italian nationalist leader Giuseppe Garibaldi.

clue.text: Embassy official has a dry ache

blocks.note: taken as written
TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomat complains of a dull pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a member of an ambassador's staff with a particular area of responsibility.

clue.text: Annoyance caused by brutal dog, real yet false

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so these letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A savage dog causes irritation, though its fierceness is somehow fake.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names anything that provokes fury, from the cloth supposedly enraging a charging animal in the ring.

clue.text: British Broadcasting Corporation looking both ways

indicators.note: something that looks the same both ways reads identically forwards and backwards

blocks.note: the informal British nickname for the broadcaster, from its initials

explanation.surface: The national broadcaster checks left and right before crossing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is the informal British nickname for the BBC, and it reads the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeb is a colloquial nickname for the national public broadcaster, formed from the initials.

clue.text: Elite aroma stirred up to become better

indicators.note: a mixture stirred up is churned into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine scent is whisked about so that it improves.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve, either making something better or growing better oneself.

clue.text: Very large nurse in north-west Belgium

definitions.note: a location standing for the place found there

blocks.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
to nurse is to look after or tend

explanation.surface: A huge nurse is working somewhere in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a port city on the Belgian coast, in the north-western province of West Flanders.

clue.text: Syndicate support to return a phone call

blocks.note: a ring is a group working together, such as a criminal syndicate
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A business syndicate offers backing in order to call someone again.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring back is British phrasing for calling a person who has phoned you earlier.

clue.text: Clergyman's residence keeps crime concealed by messenger

indicators.note: something concealed by another thing is hidden inside it

blocks.note: a page is a boy who carries messages
arson is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: A vicar's house hides a crime that a messenger is covering up.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest, the parson, to live in.

clue.text: Shocked to see spur used wildly on frenzied rides

indicators.note: something used wildly is thrown about without order
a frenzied thing is wildly agitated, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An onlooker is appalled at a rider spurring a horse hard on frantic gallops.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken aback or astonished by something unexpected is a milder form of shock.

clue.text: Armada to beat a retreat on time

blocks.note: to beat a retreat is to run away
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The Spanish Armada turning tail in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large group of warships, which is what a navy's fleet is.

clue.text: Cherish the playful oread

indicators.note: something playful frolics about, so the letters move around

blocks.note: an oread is a mountain nymph in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Someone dotes on a frolicking mountain nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to love and hold them dear, which is to worship or love deeply.

clue.text: What makes Dr Round pout and leave?

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician called Dr Round sulks and walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: Round looks like the doctor's surname but is the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop out is to withdraw from a course or activity before finishing it.

clue.text: Cold train crash, so it is believed

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the adjective: relating to what is believed

indicators.note: in a crash things are smashed and end up in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report of a rail accident in freezing weather, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrinal concerns a doctrine, a body of teachings held as creed or faith by a group.

clue.text: MP kept in right time to the instrument

indicators.note: something kept in a container is held inside it

blocks.note: true means right or correct
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A politician is held in custody until the band strikes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like the abbreviation R, but here it is TRUE, which holds MP.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet is a brass wind instrument played by buzzing the lips into a cup mouthpiece.

clue.text: Fat Ida turns up to act

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to pose is to put on an act

explanation.surface: An overweight woman named Ida arrives ready to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for animal fat, as in adipose tissue stored under the skin.

clue.text: One enters in vehicle without success

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into a car but gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in vain means doing it fruitlessly, with no useful result.

clue.text: Opening ball used to enter

definitions.note: a description standing for the noun: a thing used for entering

blocks.note: a door is an opening into a room or building
a knob is a round, ball-shaped lump

explanation.surface: At the start of a dance, guests are let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening ball' looks like the first dance of a season; it is two words read separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the round handle you turn to open a door and go through it.

clue.text: The funfair hasn't started, which is not just

indicators.note: something that has not started is missing its beginning, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains it is a shame that the fair is not yet open.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust treatment is treatment that is unfair, lacking equity or fairness.

clue.text: Little Alfred put up with taxman's skill

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Alf is a short form of the name Alfred
IR stands for Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A boy named Alfred has to tolerate the tax inspector's talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or talent for doing something well.

clue.text: Fish to swallow most quietly, which is rubbish

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

blocks.note: a cod is a fish
taken as written
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Advice to gulp down a fish silently is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' looks like an intensifier for quietly, but it trims the last letter of swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is a British colloquialism for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Mother returns OK, but in a frenzy

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so read backwards

blocks.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum comes home safe but in a wild state.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means behaving wildly and uncontrollably, out of all restraint.

clue.text: Pupil becoming half-deaf in stunt

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two halves
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolchild loses some hearing while performing a daredevil feat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is someone being taught, at school or by a tutor, as a learner is.

clue.text: Big name, Edward, kicked off

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity, a big name
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A famous figure called Edward began the football match.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick off is an idiom for beginning something, from the start of a football match.
